dn18:2.2: “It seems the Buddha is explaining the rebirths of devotees all over the nations; the Kāsis and Kosalans, Vajjis and Mallas, Cetīs and Vacchas, Kurus and Pañcālas, Macchas and Sūrasenas:
dn18:2.3: ‘This one was reborn here, while that one was reborn there.
dn18:2.4: Over fifty devotees in Ñātika have passed away having ended the five lower fetters. They’ve been reborn spontaneously, and will be extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.
dn18:2.5: More than ninety devotees in Ñātika have passed away having ended three fetters, and weakened greed, hate, and delusion. They’re once-returners, who will come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.
dn18:2.6: More than five hundred devotees in Ñātika have passed away having ended three fetters. They’re stream-enterers, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.’”

dn18:5.9: But sir, there were also Magadhan devotees—many, and of long standing too—who have passed away.
dn18:5.10: You’d think that Aṅga and Magadha were empty of devotees who have passed away!
dn18:5.11: But they too, sir, had confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and had fulfilled their ethics. The Buddha hasn’t declared their passing.
dn18:5.12: It would be good to do so, for many people would gain confidence, and so be reborn in a good place.
dn18:5.13: And sir, that King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha was a just and principled king who benefited the brahmins and householders, and people of town and country.
dn18:5.15: ‘That just and principled king, who made us so happy, has passed away.
dn18:5.16: Life was good under his dominion.’
dn18:6.1: He too, sir, had confidence in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and had fulfilled his ethics.
dn18:6.3: ‘Until his dying day, King Bimbisāra sang the Buddha’s praises!’
dn18:6.4: The Buddha hasn’t declared his passing.
dn18:6.5: It would be good to do so, for many people would gain confidence, and so be reborn in a good place.
dn18:6.6: Besides, sir, the Buddha was awakened in Magadha;
dn18:6.7: so why, sir, hasn’t he declared the rebirth of the Magadhan devotees?
dn18:6.8: If the Buddha fails to do so, sir, the Magadhan devotees will be disheartened;
dn18:7.5: “their destiny, where they were reborn in the next life.”

dn18:17.5: In the same way, when the divinity Sanaṅkumāra appears to the gods of the thirty-three, he outshines the other gods in beauty and glory.
dn18:18.2: In the same way, the god on whose couch the divinity Sanaṅkumāra sits is overjoyed and brimming with happiness.
dn18:23.11: In the same way, for one who lives aloof from sensual pleasures and unskillful qualities there arises pleasure, and more than pleasure, happiness.
dn18:24.6: In the same way, when coarse physical, verbal, and mental processes die down there arises pleasure, and more than pleasure, happiness.
dn18:25.5: They truly understand: ‘This is blameworthy, this is blameless; this should be cultivated, this should not be cultivated; this is inferior, this is superior; this has a portion of dark and bright.’
dn18:25.9: In the same way, with the fading away of ignorance and the arising of knowledge there arises pleasure, and more than pleasure, happiness.
